days.label: Friday
days.text: Friday night belongs to the waterfront and the South End. Grand Point North is back at Waterfront Park for three days, and tonight's main stage has The Devil Makes Three at 5:30, then Portugal. The Man at 7 and Grace Potter closing from 8:45 ($90 for the day, kids 12 and under free with an adult). Over on Pine Street, Oktoberfest Vermont fills the Coal Collective lot at 377 Pine with doors at 5:30 and beer flowing from 6 to 10, plus a seven piece German band, stein holding, axe throwing and a best dressed contest, 21 and up ($50 day of). I do believe I’ll be there tonight, and thanks Max for the tickets! Downtown, Cheese the Day lines Church Street from 5 to 8 with free tastings from more than 20 Vermont creameries, a wine garden at Pascolo and live music from Trio Gusto. Momo's Market Block Party runs 4 to 7 at Pomeroy Park with Barbacoa playing, Foam Brewers pouring and grilled cheese for sale, and in South Burlington the Common Roots Farm Tour walks the South Village garden beds at 4.

days.label: Saturday
days.text: Saturday starts with us. BTown Coffee Club [MEETUP] meets at Zero Gravity at 10, and at 11 our own Bike the Causeway [MEETUP] ride leaves from ECHO for close to 26 miles out the causeway, across to South Hero on the bike ferry and back, with rest stops along the way and nobody left behind. The ferry runs 10 to 6 on Saturdays this fall. From there the day is stacked. The Burlington Farmers Market runs 9 to 2 at 345 Pine Street, and the Burlington Vintage Market Fall Flea sets up next door at Barge Canal Market for the same hours with 15 vendors. Downtown, Latin American Connection kicks off with a Sambatucada parade from the top of Church Street at noon and fills City Hall Park with free music and dance until 9, including a dance class at 7 and Alma Picante at 8. The Green Mountain Book Festival takes over Phoenix Books with a nature writing workshop with Ethan Tapper at 10 and free panels on forests at 11, climate writing at 1:30 and environmental policy at 3, then wraps with Tapper's keynote at Fletcher Free Library at 7, free with registration. Party on the Bricks is back at the Opera Block on Church Street from 3:30 to 6, with Jenni Johnson & The Junketeers starting at 4.

days.label: Saturday
days.text: Saturday night is just as full. World Ballet Company brings Swan Lake to the Flynn at 7 with a cast of 50 dancers, and Grand Point North opens its doors at 2 for a day that includes Jackson Browne, Dawes, Trampled By Turtles and Grace Potter. Oktoberfest does its second night from 4:30 to 9. The Big Cheese screens at Main Street Landing at 5, a documentary about American cheesemongers competing in France that comes with a fondue reception and a Q&A ($29). In Winooski, Green Mountain Wrestling puts on free lucha libre at Four Quarters Brewing at 5:30, and they would like you to bring a chair. 90 Proof plays the beer garden at Switchback from 5:30 to 8:30, the Baroque Festival continues with Vivaldi concerti at College Street Congregational Church at 7:30, Boston songwriter Ava Sophia plays a house concert in a Burlington home from 6 to 8 ($14), and Einstein's Tap House has a Comedy Showcase at 8.

days.label: Sunday
days.text: Sunday is the one to plan around the rain. The Vermont Cheesemakers Festival at Shelburne Farms is sold out with no tickets at the door, and if you are one of the lucky ones, Bay Road is closed for construction so all festival traffic detours through Harbor Road. Grand Point North closes out with Dark Star Orchestra and Dogs In A Pile. The Forever 38 group is apple picking [MEETUP] at Shelburne Orchards at 11, and the band Sunday Morning plays the orchard at noon. The Sunday Polo Match at Amdez Polo Club in Shelburne starts at 3, and you are invited to pack a tailgate picnic. The Winooski Farmers Market runs 10 to 2, the Strange Little Market sets up 20 plus vintage clothing and local art vendors on the front lawn of the Unitarian church at the top of Church Street from 1:30 to 6, and Vermont Comedy Club hosts its Drag Brunch at 11. The free Vermont Kidney Association Walk starts at 9 in Williston, RunVermont's Island Vines 10K & 5K goes off at 9 at Snow Farm Vineyard in South Hero with only a few spots left, and the Vermont Youth Orchestra Association throws a free Community Barbecue with lawn games and music at the Elley-Long Music Center from noon to 4. Third Act Vermont marks Constitution Day with A Celebration of Press Freedom and Free Speech at the Film House at 1:30, free, with FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez and VTDigger founder Anne Galloway among the speakers. The Baroque Festival finishes with Handel's Israel in Egypt at UVM Recital Hall at 2. Sunday night, Of Monsters and Men play Higher Ground's final outdoor show of the season at Shelburne Museum with doors at 6, comedian Brad Williams is at the Flynn at 7, and Jensen McRae is at Higher Ground with doors at 7:30.
